for_you_if: you love solving intricate environmental puzzles
not_for_you_if: you are bothered by technical bugs and crashes
you dislike backtracking for full completion

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Players encounter technical bugs and challenging combat controls.

claims.claim: Reviewers report technical bugs such as breaking animations, invisible ropes, black textures, and dead scripts that can require restarting checkpoints or using unorthodox methods to progress.

citations.review_text: Story more ambitious than the previous but riddled with bugs. Animations frequently break and some sequences break resulting in repeated deaths untill you use unorthadox methods to progress.

Cool game, but unfortunately full of bugs. Black textures, invisible ropes, unusable interactables, dead scripts, and somehow some enemies just become invincible until you restart from checkpoint.

Anyway, still worth playing - maybe you'll be luckier than me and everything will actually work.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the combat system as featuring difficult combat controls, hard-to-stabilize crosshairs, and challenging weapon recoil.

citations.review_text: Not as crazy as the first one (2013 the one i'm talking), but still good regardless. Control wise, i love this game even though the combat is not that competitive compared to the 2013 one. 8/10 for 7hrs game.

Pros: Really cool and interactive game, has insane parkour and grappling features, along with great gadgets and gear which can be upgraded tremendously. The context of the story is really interesting and kind of distinctive, unlike other open world campaign games. In addition, one thing that makes this game amazing is the parkour and movement features. Furthermore, the game forces you into puzzles and pattern recognition problems for you to solve, there are many upgrades to master, on rifles, pistols, combat bows, SMG's, knifes, axes, mountain climbing equipment etc. You also require to master Lara Croft's knowledge on Greek&Persian and movesets.

Cons (May differ according to different individuals): Hard combat features, cover movement and sloppy or fast, the recoil and crosshair of the weapons are really hard to stabilize, although you can bite through it or practice your combat skills.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Players praise rewarding tombs while noting platforming precision issues, physics glitches, and technical bugs.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience physics bugs and glitches, such as erratic boat movement in the Geothermal Valley tomb.

citations.review_text:
Mechanics is worse than the first game. There are huge bugs which do affect our play style. Moreover, learning a codex is beyond the idea of "Raider" I guess and it definitely decreases the joy of the game. Besides these, achieving %100 game completion is too frustrating. Not hard, but it is a slaveish process. 
In the game there are two major chapters which are "Soviet Installation" and "Geothermal Valley" both of which made it difficult to play the game for me due to the performance issues. On the other hand, "Craft Manor" is a good DLC for players who want learn more about the protagonist. However, for players like me, who just skip all the relic/document/mural information because they are gibberish, this game is more boring then the first game. I did not like the fact that you have to go upper mountain and then shore in the first game. When you looked at this ♥♥♥♥ you just wander around to just discover a ♥♥♥♥ that is already known by the village or someone. In other words, script was too bad and there were so many unnecessary things that we have to do. Even though I just finished the main story and Blood Ties DLC, I won't be able to play the game anymore. It is too long for such a genre. 
The fighting mechanics might be the only thing that the game is good at.

Review: Rise of the Tomb Raider

I really enjoyed my time with Rise of the Tomb Raider. I finished the story with 100% completion, and overall, I’d definitely recommend the game. The exploration, story, environments, and gameplay kept me hooked all the way through.
That being said, there are a few things that definitely stood out to me and not always in a good way.

The physics can be pretty messy at times, and I encountered several bugs during my playthrough. Most of them were harmless, but some were annoying enough to take me out of the experience. For example the one Tomb with the boats in Geothermal Valley, where the boats keep 'going crazy', whenever you attach the boats to the ropes that makes you pull your own hair from frustration.

On the other hand, some of the bugs were funny. I encountered enemies randomly T-posing in the middle of the game, which was already funny enough. But somehow Lara herself decided to join in once, and I got a rare T-posing Lara Croft. Definitely not the most intimidating version of Lara I've ever seen.

As for the Baba Yaga: The Temple of the Witch DLC, I thought it was a short but enjoyable addition to the game. It doesn't take particularly long to complete, but I liked the atmosphere and the change of pace. Definitely worth playing if you already own the game.

Despite the physics issues and occasional bugs, I had a great time with Rise of the Tomb Raider. The problems didn't ruin the experience for me, and finishing the game at 100% is probably the best indication of how much I enjoyed it. I'll try to get all the Steam Achievements, but I doubt that I will ever reach the goal of getting all of them lol

Overall: It's a great Tomb Raider adventure with some questionable physics and unexpectedly funny bugs. It's a 10/10 for me and I would recommend the game for anyone that are into the Lara Croft games or just like puzzle, parkour and action games in general.

Very nice game but I feel like the story should've been a bit longer and explained things better (being vague to avoid spoilers). Though you could argue that the plot was just a way to develop Lara more than anything else so it wasn't as important, and that's fair enough. I wasn't expecting it to be as short as the first one, it's around the same, maybe a little bit longer. But it might feel longer because there is a lot more side content than in the first one.
I'm not sure if that was sacrificed to make the awful secondary game modes like score attack or Lara's Nightmare. 
The Croft Manor dlc was very cool, but it could've easily been part of the prologue.
The Baba Yaga dlc was... meh, I kinda hated the final part.

I 100%'d it in survivor diff and found the combat to be a bit annoying, so many armoured enemies that could overwhelm you at any time, but maybe that's on me as I wasn't quite sure what was good against those, except special arrows, but I didn't wanna be using the bow all the time. Also, melee isn't QTE ♥♥♥♥ like in the previous game, but it's still clunky and awful.

I had some physics issues with high fps, but nothing really gamebreaking and it was mostly visual (the worst one being the grapple hook not showing where it actually is at all, even tho it works properly). But if you don't wanna have any, cap the game at around 100 fps. That's around the amount of fps where I wasn't seeing any visual bugs.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the optional tombs and puzzles as a major highlight, praising their design and the rewards they provide.

citations.review_text:
Rise of the Tomb Raider — an adventure that still holds up surprisingly well.

The environments, weather effects, lighting, and tombs looks absolutely stunning even by today's standards. It's hard to believe this game is over a decade old.

The story is engaging from start to finish, with Lara growing into the badass we all know. It does feel a little rushed in places (especially towards the ending) but it's still a fantastic adventure.

The tombs are easily one of the highlights. I loved solving the puzzles, although I wish they relied more on actual interaction instead of pressing Q and E every few seconds. Still, exploring ancient ruins never gets old.

Not everything landed though... The Big Bad Old Smelly Baba Yaga DLC starts as one of the creepiest and most intriguing side stories, only to end with "oh... it's just some b*tch-ass old granny who lost her mind." The payoff simply wasn't worth the build-up.

There were also moments where Lara suddenly turned into Ezio Auditore da Firenze. Some of the parkour and physics made me question whether I was playing Tomb Raider or Assassin's Creed... nothing game-breaking, just unintentionally funny.

Blood Ties addition was a pleasant surprise. Even though you're mostly exploring Croft Manor and collecting bunch of crap, it expands Lara's family story beautifully and gives much more insight into her parents and their legacy.

The only thing I genuinely hated were the achievement-related challenges. I don't think I've ever played a game with challenges this long, repetitive, and painfully unfun. They felt like complete bullsh*t where they existed solely to waste your damn time rather than test your skills.

Despite that, Rise of the Tomb Raider is an excellent adventure. Would I play it again in a few years? Absolutely. But only for the main campaign — the story, exploration, and tombs are more than worth coming back for. The rest... can stay buried.

By far the HARDEST of the trilogie. I died so many times against enemies and the last boss fight tops all three games. Cool level design, felt like a historical fantasy movie and it had the best, most original and most fun challenge/optional tombs of all! However I also experienced the most bugs, especially farming animal skins was near impossible with its buggy respawn mechanic. The NPCs and story were better than on the island, it had way more substance, however not as well thought out as Shadow of the Tomb Raider. Several plot holes in the story but i still had lots of fun. The outfits can't compete with Shadow unfortunately, very boring or poorly designed, offering little variety.

At the time of beating the main story and 100%ing a save I'd say this has become one of my favourite story games ever. The combat is incredible, killing enemies and animals with a bow and arrow literally never gets old and I loved all of the enemy encounters as well as hunting in general. The story was great and genuinely very gripping and interesting. Lara is a phenomenal character and easily one of the best main characters ever. Exploration is outstanding, the tombs and crypts are fun to solve and actually give you rewards that you can't get elsewhere in the game, making it very easy for me to wander off from the story missions and explore between the story. 

There is some little grips I have of the game which I'll speed through: although movement genuinely feels very responsive as a whole, the climbing specifically can be very jank in some sections, and even after a climbing speed upgrade it's pretty slow. The game seems to have a bad achievement detection and there was 3 times I should have got achievements when I didn't, like the achievement for beating the first level of the game, that I had to use an un-locker just to get. The wire spool upgrade is the worst designed part of this game by a landslide, yes it's essential to the game and makes some previous areas trivial by being able to reach ledges from much further away, however I feels like a large portion of the game wasn't designed with the upgrade in mind and there's a few instances where it just doesn't interact with the map as you would expect it to which feels like ♥♥♥♥ when it happens and is extremely frustrating. I also found that some areas don't backtrack very well, I get that it can be hard for games with a full open world that has the missions set in the same areas as the free roam, but too many sections don't make an effort to give you a method to backtrack to assist in retrieving all collectables.

I went into this game wanting to 100% it, and until today I still thought I would be able to…

A few spots where its hilariously easy to get out of bounds, not that you can take advantage of that in any way. Like they forgot to put any kind of invisible wall. (I mean theres absolutely nothing there and its not worth your time because its in a already completed area.)

Combat is piss easy and I only ever used cartable items for ♥♥♥♥♥ n giggles. You can just shoot people, theres never any reason to use distractions. Sometimes theres a group of enemies and you can just use a moltov to kill them all I guess. Maybe on the hardest difficulties they're worth using but I doubt it?
Seems like I just had the best weapons from the start cus I had the complete edition or something? Suppose you could use the worse weapons if you wanted to?

Sometimes when I try to make a jump Lara will just jump in the opposite direction to her death for no damn reason. (Built in game length padding system? You be the judge.)

citations.review_text:

In my opinion, the best installment of the Survivor Trilogy.

Same as with Tomb Raider 2013, the semi-open world is greatly designed. Good balance of exploration, challenges, puzzles and story.

If you enjoyed the previous game, you'll most likely enjoy this one too.

The only really negative thing about Rise of the Tomb Raider, for me at least, is the HUGE amount of back-tracking you'll have to do to complete the game at 100%. Lots of areas are locked-out when you first encounter them because of missing tools and skills etc. Just a minor gripe, but I'm not a big fan of this approach. 

Recommendation: Get the "Tomb Raider: Definitive Survivor Trilogy " if it's heavily discounted (80-90% off). Well worth it then.
